items.title: HDP: A Lightweight Cryptographic Protocol for Human Delegation Provenance in Agentic AI Systems
items.target_h2: 从“文本是否恶意”到“谁获得了行为控制权”
items.target_ref: books/part-06-ai-infrastructure/72-security.md#L240 (H2: 从“文本是否恶意”到“谁获得了行为控制权”)
items.mechanism_delta: HDP 用可验证 token 将 human principal、delegate、scope 与 append-only delegation chain 绑定，并在终端执行前验证；authorization owner 从 prompt/agent 自述迁移到可核验 provenance chain 与执行 gate。
items.changed_constraint: 现有 tool token 或 agent identity 常只证明当前调用者，低层级委托时足够；多跳 delegation 出现后，终端 action 无法证明最初 human principal、完整委托链与每跳 scope。
items.tradeoffs_failure_fallback: 收益是补足多跳 human authorization accountability；代价是 key/token 生命周期、撤销、重放与 scope 组合复杂度。它不替代 prompt-injection、行为正确性或运行时 sandbox；token 不完整或验证失败时应 fail closed 并回退人工授权。
items.evidence_boundary: `HDP: A Lightweight Cryptographic Protocol for Human Delegation Provenance in Agentic AI Systems` 只证明 exact-v1 的公开模型、数据、硬件和 workload；evaluation evidence 为：We situate HDP within the existing landscape of delegation protocols, identify its distinct design point relative to OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange (RFC 8693), JSON Web Tokens (RFC 7519), UCAN, and the Intent Provenance Protocol (draft-haberkamp-ipp-00), and demonstrate that existing standards fail to address the multi-hop, append-only, human-provenance requirements of agentic systems. 未披露生产 SLO、多租户、跨硬件或长期运行结果时，不得外推。
items.suggested_insertion: 在 `从“文本是否恶意”到“谁获得了行为控制权”` 的演进主线内、章末小结与 Review notes 前整合。

items.title: Hardware-Level Governance of AI Compute: A Feasibility Taxonomy for Regulatory Compliance and Treaty Verification
items.target_h2: 从资产与信任边界开始
items.target_ref: books/part-06-ai-infrastructure/72-security.md#L16 (H2: 从资产与信任边界开始)
adjacent_refs: books/part-06-ai-infrastructure/73-production-best-practice.md#L31 (H2: Demo 证明可能性，生产承担证明责任)
items.mechanism_delta: 论文以 adversary tier 区分 commercial、non-state 与 nation-state threat，并把目标从 tamper-proof 改为 tamper-evident assurance；attestation owner 管理测量对象、硬件根、证据链、对手假设与可声明的合规边界。
items.changed_constraint: 算力治理常假设硬件可以提供绝对防篡改计量；在商业合规且对手能力有限时可作为近似，但非国家与国家级对手会改变传感器、固件和审计链的可信边界。
items.tradeoffs_failure_fallback: 收益是让监管/条约验证选择与对手能力匹配的硬件机制；代价是供应链信任、远程证明、隐私和误判。无法保证绝对不可绕过，证据链缺失或 threat tier 超界时应缩小结论并回退现场/多方审计，而不是把硬件信号当最终事实。
items.evidence_boundary: `Hardware-Level Governance of AI Compute: A Feasibility Taxonomy for Regulatory Compliance and Treaty Verification` 只证明 exact-v1 的公开模型、数据、硬件和 workload；evaluation evidence 为：Not Disclosed — 摘要未给出足以跨 workload 复算的完整 evaluation matrix；正文实验仍只按 exact-v1 范围引用。 未披露生产 SLO、多租户、跨硬件或长期运行结果时，不得外推。
items.suggested_insertion: 在 `从资产与信任边界开始` 的演进主线内、章末小结与 Review notes 前整合。

items.title: Blind-Spot Mass: A Good-Turing Framework for Quantifying Deployment Coverage Risk in Machine Learning Systems
items.target_h2: 第二个不变量：评估结论总是相对于分布
items.target_ref: books/part-06-ai-infrastructure/66-evaluation-system.md#L170 (H2: 第二个不变量：评估结论总是相对于分布)
items.mechanism_delta: Blind-Spot Mass 用 Good-Turing 估计支持度低于阈值的总概率质量，并把 overall performance 分解为 supported 与 blind components；evaluation owner 必须保存 support threshold、样本分布、估计不确定性与 release decision。
items.changed_constraint: 部署评估通常用平均准确率与已见切片估计覆盖；分布轻尾且样本充分时可用，但 heavy-tailed operational states 中大量低频/未见状态会让测试分数掩盖 coverage risk。
items.tradeoffs_failure_fallback: 收益是把未见/低支持状态从模糊担忧变成受 distribution contract 约束的 release-risk signal；代价是阈值敏感、独立同分布假设和估计方差。分布漂移或样本依赖破坏假设时，应回退分层抽样、在线 canary 与保守 release gate，论文推导不等于生产风险上界。
items.evidence_boundary: `Blind-Spot Mass: A Good-Turing Framework for Quantifying Deployment Coverage Risk in Machine Learning Systems` 只证明 exact-v1 的公开模型、数据、硬件和 workload；evaluation evidence 为：In modern ML systems, operational state distributions are often heavy-tailed, implying that a long tail of valid but rare states is structurally under-supported in finite training and evaluation data. We further derive a coverage-imposed accuracy ceiling, decomposing overall performance into supported and blind components and separating capacity limits from data limits. 未披露生产 SLO、多租户、跨硬件或长期运行结果时，不得外推。
items.suggested_insertion: 在 `第二个不变量：评估结论总是相对于分布` 的演进主线内、章末小结与 Review notes 前整合。
